first_record.description: 1. Patient, male, 61 years old, admitted for 'cough with blood-tinged sputum for >1 month.' 2. Denies history of hypertension, coronary artery disease, diabetes, hepatitis, tuberculosis, or close contact with TB. Denies major trauma, surgery, or blood transfusion. No known food or drug allergies. Vaccination history per local records. 3. Physical Exam: Trachea midline, bilateral supraclavicular lymph nodes not palpably enlarged. Chest symmetrical, bilateral respiratory excursion equal, bilateral tactile fremitus normal. Percussion of bilateral lungs is resonant. Bilateral breath sounds clear, no obvious dry or moist crackles/rhonchi, no pleural friction rub. 4. Ancillary Tests: Chest CT on 2025-11-29 showed: right upper lobe mass, mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy, and chronic pulmonary inflammation.

first_record.differential_diagnosis: 1. Lung Cancer: Elderly male, chest CT suggests left upper lung nodule with ill-defined margins; pulmonary malignancy cannot be ruled out, pending postoperative pathology for definitive diagnosis. 2. Inflammatory Pseudotumor: Most patients are under 50, often with a history of respiratory tract infections. May be asymptomatic or have intermittent fever, cough, sputum, and occasionally hemoptysis. X-ray shows round or oval solitary mass shadow, medium density, uniform texture, ill-defined margins, occasionally with pleural adhesion, mostly in the lung periphery. Based on history and CT, this cannot be excluded, pending pathology. 3. Tuberculoma: Predilection for apical/posterior segments of upper lobes and superior segments of lower lobes. Uniform density, possible calcification, satellite lesions around the focus. Patients often have systemic symptoms like low-grade fever, fatigue, night sweats. Patient denies TB history/contact. Systemic anti-TB treatment for half a year showed no significant change on follow-up CT; thus, this is less likely. Definitive diagnosis requires pathology.
first_record.plan: 1. Complete relevant workup to determine the nature of the mass; 2. Active preoperative preparation for elective surgery; 3. Consult attending physician for treatment guidance.

other_records.record_content: Patient has occasional cough, blood-tinged sputum, no fever or chest tightness. Exam: Bilateral breath sounds decreased, no crackles. Reviewed ancillary tests. Diagnosis: Pulmonary space-occupying lesion. Recommendation: Scheduled for bronchoscopy tomorrow (with EBUS if necessary), sign consent, NPO pre-op, monitor BP and SpO2.

Day 3 post-admission. Alert, good spirit, afebrile, no chest pain/tightness, no nausea/vomiting. Good diet, sleep, normal bowel/bladder function. Exam: Trachea midline, chest symmetrical, equal excursion, normal fremitus, resonant percussion, decreased breath sounds bilaterally, no crackles/rubs. Underwent bronchoscopy today. Awaiting pathology results to determine next treatment steps. Continue monitoring and symptomatic management.

Procedure: Bronchoscopy. Time: 2025-12-03 11:02. Steps: Transnasal insertion. Tracheal lumen patent, mucosa hypertrophic, carina sharp. Left main and left lower lobe bronchi contained copious grayish-white mucoid sputum; cleared, lumen patent. Left upper lobe mucosa hypertrophic, carina blunted. Lingula unremarkable. Apicoposterior and anterior segments of LUL narrowed, mucosa hypertrophic; neoplasm visible on the wall of the apicoposterior segment. Right main/intermediate bronchi patent, no neoplasm. RUL bronchial orifice mucosa rough and hypertrophic; anterior segment bronchus obstructed by neoplasm, compressing apical segment, bronchoscope cannot pass. Posterior segment of RUL patent. Biopsies taken from RUL anterior segment and LUL apicoposterior segment orifices. No active bleeding, suctioned and withdrawn smoothly. Result: Procedure completed smoothly, vitals stable. Pathology: (LUL) Consistent with squamous cell carcinoma (limited tissue). (RUL) Squamous cell carcinoma (moderately differentiated). IHC: P40(+), TTF-1(-), Ki-67(~70%), HER2(0), BRAF V600E(-), c-MET(1+, weak >90%), TROP2(moderate 40%, weak 60%). Post-op: NPO 2h, O2, cardiac monitoring.

Patient, male, 61yo, admitted for cough with blood-tinged sputum. CT showed RUL mass encasing pulmonary artery, unresectable. Bronchoscopy on 12-03 showed bilateral lung masses... Pathology confirmed SCC. Patient has bilateral lung malignancies, unresectable, recommended for comprehensive anti-tumor therapy (chemo). Family understood and agreed. Transferring for treatment. Current status: No obvious discomfort, cough/sputum improved.

Reviewed transfer-out record. Current Diagnosis: 1. Right lung malignancy (SCC cT4N2M1 Stage IV) 2. Secondary lung malignancy 3. Secondary mediastinal LN malignancy 4. Secondary hilar LN malignancy 5. Pneumonia. Plan: 1. Internal medicine routine... 3. Comprehensive anti-tumor therapy. 4. Padua VTE risk assessment: High risk. Educated on VTE prophylaxis, hydration, ambulation. Bilateral LE venous US recommended to rule out DVT, patient temporarily refused. Bleeding risk for medical VTE prophylaxis assessed as high; withholding LMWH for now, monitoring for bleeding, serial D-dimer.

Brief history: 61yo male, cough with hemoptysis. Indication: Requires long-term infusion of hypertonic/vesicant chemo drugs, peripheral IV access difficult, indication for TIVAP. Procedure: TIVAP placement. Anesthesia: Local. Risks: US-guided puncture to avoid complications, DSA for catheter tip positioning... Pre-op assessment: Vitals stable, coagulation normal, subcutaneous fat thickness and skin condition evaluated. Surgeon evaluated patient, confirmed indication, no contraindications. Scheduled for 2025-12-09.

Surgery completed 09:40. Supine position, right chest wall exposed, prepped/draped. 2% lidocaine local infiltration. US-guided puncture of right axillary vein, 0.035-inch guidewire, 7F peel-away sheath. Fluoroscopy guided catheter to cavoatrial junction. Sheath removed. 2.5cm incision, subcutaneous pocket created, port connected and placed. Huber needle inserted, aspiration smooth, pulse flush. Sutured, dressed. Patient tolerated well, returned to ward.

ward_records.content: Patient stable, occasional cough/hemoptysis. Pulm consult for bronchoscopy. VTE prophylaxis education.
Path confirmed SCC. Unresectable. Recommended chemo. Family agreed to transfer.
Diagnosis clear, Stage IV, no surgical indication. Plan: Gemcitabine 1.2g d1,d5 + Cisplatin 40mg d1-2, 20mg d3 + Sintilimab 200mg. Symptomatic tx.
TIVAP placed today. Tolerated well. Proceed with chemo+IO.
Labs/Imaging reviewed (Brain MRI: multiple ischemic foci; Sputum culture: normal flora). Continue current tx.
Labs reviewed (CBC, Cortisol, ACTH, Thyroid). Chemo+IO completed. Tolerated well. Cleared for discharge.

enter_record.body_examination: T 36C P 84 bpm R 21 bpm BP 145/83 mmHg H 168 cm W 66 kg. VTE Risk: Low. Nutritional Risk: 0. Elderly male, normal development, moderate nutrition, alert, autonomous position, cooperative. Skin: no jaundice, petechiae, or hemorrhagic spots. Superficial lymph nodes: not palpably enlarged. Head: normal development, uniform hair distribution. Eyes: no eyelid edema, conjunctival congestion, or scleral icterus; pupils equal and round, light and accommodation reflexes present. Ears/Nose: unremarkable. Mouth: no cyanosis of lips, pharyngeal congestion, or tonsillar enlargement. Neck: soft, no resistance, no jugular venous distension, no carotid bruits, trachea midline, thyroid not enlarged. Chest: symmetrical, no deformities. Lungs: clear breath sounds, no dry or moist crackles. Heart: no precordial bulge, heart border not enlarged, HR 84 bpm, regular rhythm, no pathological murmurs. Abdomen: flat, soft, no tenderness or rebound tenderness. Liver/spleen not palpable. Murphy's sign negative. No percussion pain in liver/kidney regions. Bowel sounds normal. No shifting dullness. Spine/Extremities: no deformities, no lower extremity edema. Dorsalis pedis pulses normal. Reflexes: biceps, patellar, and abdominal reflexes normal. Babinski and Brudzinski signs negative.
enter_record.complain: Cough with blood-tinged sputum for over 1 month.
enter_record.family: Parents deceased, details unknown. Denies family history of genetic or infectious diseases.
enter_record.marriage: Married at appropriate age, 1 son, spouse and child healthy.
enter_record.past: Denies history of hypertension, coronary artery disease, diabetes, hepatitis, tuberculosis, or close contact with TB. Denies major trauma, surgery, or blood transfusion. No known food or drug allergies. Vaccination history per local records.
enter_record.personal: Born and raised locally, no long-term exposure to toxins, industrial dust, or radiation. Denies travel to endemic areas. Denies high-risk sexual behavior. Smoking history: 50+ years, 3 packs/day; Alcohol history: 40+ years, ~500g/day.
enter_record.present: The patient developed a cough with blood-tinged sputum of unknown etiology over 1 month ago, occasionally accompanied by right hypochondriac pain. Denies dyspnea, night sweats, fatigue, palpitations, shortness of breath, belching, acid reflux, burning sensation, retrosternal or shoulder pain, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, or bloating. Visited a local clinic and received oral medications and IV infusions (details unknown) with no significant improvement. Two days ago, a chest CT at Culaizhen Health Center showed: right upper lobe mass, mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy, and chronic pulmonary inflammation; no specific treatment was given. Admitted via outpatient clinic for 'Pulmonary Space-Occupying Lesion'. Since onset, diet and sleep fair, bowel/bladder normal, no significant weight loss.

exit_record.enter_description: Patient, male, 61yo, admitted for 'cough with blood-tinged sputum for >1 month'. Denies HTN, CAD, DM, hepatitis, TB. Denies major trauma/surgery. No allergies. Exam: Trachea midline, supraclavicular LNs negative. Chest symmetrical, lungs clear. CT showed RUL mass, lymphadenopathy, chronic inflammation.
out_advice: 1. Rest, enhance nutrition, avoid colds and fatigue. Repeat CBC and LFTs 7 days post-discharge. If WBC < 3.0 x 10^9/L or ANC < 1.5 x 10^9/L, administer Filgrastim (G-CSF) 100ug SC QD for 5 days. If PLT < 75 x 10^9/L, administer rhIL-11 3mg SC QD for 5 days. Recheck CBC on day 6. If WBC < 1.5 or PLT < 30, or fever occurs, contact attending physician immediately.
2. Discharge Medications: Dextromethorphan/Guaifenesin syrup 10ml TID; Esomeprazole 20mg QD; Ondansetron 8mg TID PRN for nausea/vomiting.
3. Seek immediate medical attention if fever, diarrhea, or abdominal pain occurs.
4. Return for scheduled chemotherapy. Contact ward 3-4 days in advance to reserve bed.
exit_record.out_description: Patient denies nausea, vomiting, chest tightness, pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. Diet, sleep, and bowel/bladder functions normal. Exam: Trachea midline, LNs negative. Chest symmetrical, lungs clear, no crackles or rubs.

Secondary Malignant Neoplasm of Mediastinal Lymph Nodes
Secondary Malignant Neoplasm of Hilar Lymph Nodes
exit_record.treatment: Admitted for pulmonary mass. CT showed RUL mass encasing pulmonary artery, unresectable. Bronchoscopy and biopsy confirmed bilateral SCC (P40+, TTF-1-, Ki-67 70%). Staging MRI/US/Bone scan negative for distant metastasis except local nodal involvement. Diagnosed with Stage IV SCC. TIVAP placed under US/fluoroscopy guidance without complications. Received Cycle 1 Gemcitabine + Cisplatin + Sintilimab. Tolerated well, no severe myelosuppression or organ toxicity. Discharged in stable condition.

image_reports.diagnosis: Multiple ischemic infarct foci in the brain
image_reports.findings: Multiple punctate iso/long T1 and long T2 signal foci in bilateral corona radiata, bilateral centrum semiovale, and bilateral frontal lobes. Hyperintense on T2-FLAIR. No obvious hyperintensity on DWI. Ventricular system not dilated. Sulci and fissures not widened or deepened. Midline structure centered.

Liver slightly plump, capsule smooth, parenchyma echo slightly dense, enhanced, and homogeneous. Vascular texture clear. Portal and common bile ducts not dilated. Gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, kidneys, and adrenal glands unremarkable.

image_reports.diagnosis:
Impression:
1. Right upper lobe mass, suggestive of malignancy; mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy; recommend further workup.
2. Chronic pulmonary inflammation.
3. Pulmonary nodules, recommend follow-up.
4. Partial coronary artery calcification.
image_reports.findings: Soft tissue density mass in the hilar region of the right upper lobe, local bronchial narrowing. Pulmonary nodules and cord-like/flocculent opacities. RUL nodule approx. 25mm, irregular borders. Interstitial changes. Mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy. No pleural effusion. Coronary calcification noted.

image_reports.diagnosis:
Basal septal hypertrophy
Aortic valve degeneration
image_reports.findings: Chambers normal size. Septa intact. Basal septum hypertrophic. Aortic valve thickened, echo enhanced. Mild tricuspid regurgitation. E/A < 1.

image_reports.diagnosis:
Right thyroid nodule, TI-RADS 4a
Multiple other thyroid nodules, TI-RADS 3
image_reports.findings: Right lobe 23x16mm hypoechoic nodule, ill-defined borders (TI-RADS 4a). Multiple other benign-appearing nodules. No abnormal cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
